title: dir2mcp_recheck_path
description: Ask a running server in watch mode to reconcile one path under the corpus root now, instead of at the next periodic safety rescan (bs-007). Optional extension: served only when the server runs the file watcher and is not read-only; otherwise absent from tools/list and TOOL_UNAVAILABLE on call. The call enqueues the reconcile and returns; it does not wait for ingestion. The queue is bounded: a call that would add a new pending request to a full queue fails with QUEUE_FULL (retryable).

rel_path.description: Path relative to the corpus root, with the grammar and normalization of dir2mcp_open_file's rel_path ('/' as the separator, no leading '/'). A file or a directory; '.' names the root itself. A path that resolves outside the root is PATH_OUTSIDE_ROOT. An excluded path is accepted, never stat'ed, and reported as kind 'excluded'; the reconcile retires what was indexed at it and under it. A path that does not exist is accepted: the reconcile tombstones what was indexed there.

recursive.description: For a directory: when true (default) reconcile the whole subtree; when false, only the regular files that are its direct children. Ignored for a file.

rel_path.description: The normalized corpus-relative path the request resolved to ('.' for the root).

kind.description: What the call found at call time: a regular file, a directory, nothing (missing), or excluded. excluded means ineligible: the path matches the exclusion engine's path rules, is a symlink to such a target, is a symlink the server does not follow, or is a special entry (FIFO, socket, device). A path the exclusion path rules match is never touched, so for it 'excluded' says nothing about whether anything exists there; otherwise 'excluded' shows only what the lstat checks found: a special entry, or a symlink at the path or at one of its components (a symlink component, such as alias in alias/report.txt, says nothing about whether the requested path exists). Nothing is read. With symlinks followed, a cycle or more than 40 hops also makes the path ineligible.

queued.description: true when this call added a reconcile request; false when a request for the same normalized rel_path was already pending (the queue holds at most one per path).

pending.description: Number of reconcile requests pending at the moment this call enqueued its request or found the pending one (one atomic step with the deduplication), this one included (when queued is false, the already-pending request for the same path is counted), so the value is at least 1. A worker that starts the request right after does not change the value.
